patch.value: GH-1178: history hashes exclude record author and agent provenance, so attribution can be rewritten without detection

GitHub issue #1178 reproduces on pm-cli 2026.9.2: editing a history record's ts, author, author_source, op, or agent_provenance does not alter the item patch hashes. After uncached verification, pm health --strict-exit and pm history --verify --strict-exit still report clean. The ledger therefore proves item-state replay but not the immutable attribution and operation metadata that describes who performed it.

Define a versioned canonical hash envelope covering at least timestamp, author, author_source, operation, and agent provenance; preserve explicit backward verification for legacy histories without claiming they cover attribution; supply a documented, audited migration and repair boundary; add a negative control that changes only author or provenance and must fail history verification and health; compose with re-anchoring preservation instead of erasing original evidence; pass history, merge, restore, SDK, CLI, security, static, and exact coverage gates.
pm-cli 2026.9.2 with a fresh single-entry item history stream

Create an item, edit only the stored history record author and agent_provenance fields, remove the drift cache, then run pm health --strict-exit and pm history <id> --verify --strict-exit; both exit zero.

A versioned history-integrity epoch covers immutable record metadata as well as item-state hashes, accepts legacy epochs explicitly, documents migration/repair, and rejects attribution tampering with an executable negative control.
Record attribution and operation metadata sit outside the hashed content, so they can be rewritten while the item hash chain and health gate remain clean.
Core history ledger, SDK verification, health, and repair compatibility
Reviewers and agents can receive a green integrity verdict after attribution was modified during merge, rebase, or manual repair.
